clue.text: What cook needs ready for eating outside city area

indicators.note: one word standing outside another wraps around it, holding it within

parts.note: fruit ready for eating is ripe
EC is the East Central postal district of London, home of the City

explanation.surface: A cook wants produce that is ready to eat, sourced from outside the city.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district, which falls in the East Central postal area.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook follows a set of written instructions listing ingredients and method for a dish.

clue.text: A little woman in rave beaming

indicators.note: in places one group of letters inside another word

parts.note: to rave is to rant
taken as written
Di is a short form of the name Diana

explanation.surface: A small woman at a rave, grinning from ear to ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little woman' means a woman's name cut short, here Diana.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone smiling broadly with joy looks radiant, glowing with happiness.

clue.text: Music-maker entertained by chancellor

indicators.note: entertained by means held as a guest inside, so the letters sit within the next word

parts.note: the letters sit inside this word

explanation.surface: A musician is invited to perform for the Chancellor.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowed string instrument, the cello, produces music, so it is a music-maker.

clue.text: Dad at home with item of furniture that can be given a coat of gloss?

definitions.text: that can be given a coat of gloss?

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
someone at home is in
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Father at home deciding whether a piece of furniture will take a coat of gloss paint.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as one example: gloss is one kind of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: Something able to receive paint, such as a glossy finish, is paintable.

clue.text: Soldiers getting round lake — this will provide shade

parts.note: paras are paratroopers
O is a round shape
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Troops marching around a lake look forward to some shade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting round lake' reads like the soldiers circling it, but round simply gives O, placed after PARAS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunshade umbrella is carried or set up to keep the sun off, so it gives shade.

clue.text: Exercise getting journalists into a happy mood

parts.note: the press is the body of journalists
someone feeling cheerful is up

explanation.surface: Reporters doing a workout to lift their spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A press-up, called a push-up in America, is a floor exercise lifting the body with the arms.

clue.text: Something high in cooler — first thing to be thrown out

indicators.text: first thing to be thrown out
indicators.note: says the opening letter is discarded from the word

parts.note: a fridge keeps food cool

explanation.surface: Something placed high up in the refrigerator, the first item to be thrown away.
explanation.walkthrough: FRIDGE loses its first letter F.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a long raised crest of land or a roof top, so it is elevated.

clue.text: Man reacts unexpectedly in religious ceremony

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests things turning out differently, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A man responds with surprise during a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Baptism and communion are examples of Christian rites, each called a sacrament.

clue.text: Peril ultimately with snake? Run!

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of peril
an adder is a kind of snake

explanation.surface: Faced with a dangerous snake, the only thing to do is run!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run!' looks like a command to flee; it is a run in tights. The surface also nods to the board game snakes and ladders.
explanation.definitionFit: A vertical line of unravelled stitches in stockings is a ladder in British usage, a run in American.

clue.text: Nervous in an act of brinkmanship?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, playful: standing literally at the brink

explanation.walkthrough: Brinkmanship is pushing a dangerous situation to the limit; the question mark flags a literal reading of being right at the brink.
explanation.definitionFit: Anxious people are described idiomatically as tense, and the phrase also means physically at a precipice's lip.

clue.text: Flirting daughter joins friendly group

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
an alliance is a group of friendly parties

explanation.surface: A daughter flirts as she joins a friendly circle.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual romantic trifling with someone is a dalliance, the noun for flirting or playful courtship.

clue.text: Chopped up food finally covered with sweet stuff

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word, so only its closing letter is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of food
a cake covered with sugary topping is iced

explanation.surface: Food that has been chopped up and then coated in sugar.
explanation.definitionFit: Vegetables cut into small cubes are diced, so the past participle matches chopped up.

clue.text: A fight in the vicinity

parts.note: taken as written
a boxing match is a bout

explanation.surface: A scuffle breaks out somewhere nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is around or nearby is said to be about, as in 'is he about?'.

clue.text: Dear Pete's awfully full of hopelessness

indicators.note: awfully suggests something done badly, so the letters come out in a mangled order

parts.note: the letters of these two words
the S of the possessive joins the fodder

explanation.surface: Dear old Pete is in a terribly gloomy state.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Pete counts in the fodder rather than reading as 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person in despair, having lost all hope, is described as desperate.

clue.text: Bother, finishing in airport with foreign currency

indicators.note: finishing means the very end of the next word, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of airport
the rouble is the Russian currency

explanation.surface: A traveller has hassle at the airport changing foreign money.
explanation.definitionFit: Bother and trouble are synonyms for difficulty, inconvenience or annoyance, as nouns or verbs.

clue.text: Supreme rulers finished on cricket ground

parts.note: something finished is over
Lord's is the famous London cricket ground

explanation.surface: The rulers' reign ended at a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's, in north-west London, is the home of English cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Overlords are rulers who hold power over other lords or peoples, supreme in authority.

clue.text: Harry, a snooker player?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the boy wizard of J. K. Rowling's novels, known by his surname
second meaning: someone who pots balls on the table

explanation.surface: Is someone called Harry perhaps a snooker player?
explanation.walkthrough: Harry looks like a verb (to harass) or any Harry; it is the famous fictional wizard.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry is the schoolboy wizard surname in the books, and in snooker one who sinks balls pots them.

clue.text: New entrant is fly-by-night

indicators.note: new suggests a fresh form, so the letters are made into something different

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A newcomer turns out to be unreliable and here today, gone tomorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Fly-by-night describes something short-lived or not staying long, which matches passing and temporary.

clue.text: Leave behind a land with limited opportunity for growth

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to abandon

definitions.text: a land with limited opportunity for growth
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a noun, an arid barren region where little grows

explanation.surface: Emigrants abandoning a country with poor economic prospects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Growth' reads as economic, but the second meaning is literal: little vegetation grows there.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon someone is to desert them, and a dry sandy expanse with scant plant life is a desert.

clue.text: Having the will to help others following on?

definitions.text: Having the will to help others following on

parts.words: Having the will to help others
parts.note: surface reading: being determined to do good for people
setter's reading: having made a legal will that benefits the heirs who come after one's death

explanation.surface: Someone with the determination to assist those coming along behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' reads as willpower, but it is the legal document; those following on are the heirs.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who dies having left a valid legal will is testate, the opposite of intestate.

clue.text: Last-minute note to change church book

parts.note: a postscript, added at the end of a letter
to alter is to change

explanation.surface: A late memo announcing a change to a book used in church.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Psalms printed for worship is a psalter, a volume used in church services.

clue.text: Platform bringing disgrace to president

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for president
odium is public disgrace or hatred

explanation.surface: A political platform that brings shame on the head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: ODIUM is added to P, so P comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised stand for a speaker or winner is a podium, a kind of platform.

clue.text: Members of a family are told

definitions.meaning: first meaning: what family members are to one another, kin
second meaning: recounted, as a story

explanation.surface: The family members are informed of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a sentence missing its last word: the answer completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Kin connected by blood are related, and a narrated story has been related, meaning recounted.

clue.text: Member to perform final act in story

parts.note: a limb, such as a leg, is a member of the body
to end is to do the last thing, finish

explanation.surface: A cast member is due to perform in the closing act of a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a traditional tale passed down, a story often of heroic deeds.

clue.text: European Union record is set down by editor and praised

parts.note: the usual abbreviation
a log is a written record
taken as written
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A record of EU business is written up by an editor and commended.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak or write highly of someone, typically in a tribute, is to eulogise them.

clue.text: Police officer held in regard, always

indicators.note: held in means contained, so the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters run across these two words

explanation.surface: A policeman who is always held in high regard.
explanation.walkthrough: The Garda Síochána is the police force of Ireland, and an officer in it is a garda.
explanation.definitionFit: A garda is an Irish police officer, the term taken from the force's name.

clue.text: Burglar's collection's thrown back in seat

indicators.note: thrown back means sent the other way, so the letters are read from the end

parts.note: a burglar's haul is loot
the S of the possessive is taken as a letter

explanation.surface: A thief's stolen goods are tossed back onto a chair.
explanation.walkthrough: LOOT plus S, read backwards, gives STOOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A backless seat for one person, often on legs, is a stool.

clue.text: Here's old piano — time for musical entertainment

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
p is the musical marking for piano, softly
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: An old piano is wheeled out for a night of music.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a staged drama set to music, a form of musical entertainment.

clue.text: Alarm not initially the cause of fault

indicators.note: not initially says to drop the opening letter of the word

parts.note: terror is extreme alarm

explanation.surface: A false alarm turns out to be caused by a fault.
explanation.walkthrough: TERROR loses its first letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistake or flaw, especially in a system, is called an error or fault.

clue.text: A maiden to exploit men — time for fun!

parts.note: taken as written
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over
to exploit is to use
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A young woman decides to take advantage of men, purely for her own enjoyment.
explanation.walkthrough: A maiden over in cricket is one in which no runs are scored, written M on a scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: Entertainment or enjoyment is amusement, so it serves as a noun meaning fun.

clue.text: What could be seaside illness

indicators.note: what could be suggests a possible rearrangement of the next word into something else

parts.note: the letters of this word

explanation.surface: A holiday at the coast that leaves someone sick.
explanation.definitionFit: A disease is a specific illness or disorder affecting the body.

clue.text: Something a bit ropy in London thoroughfare

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a single twisted thread of a rope
second meaning: a major street in central London

explanation.surface: A shabby, run-down street in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ropy' in British slang means poor quality; here it means literally part of a rope. The Strand is a well-known road running from Trafalgar Square towards the City.
explanation.definitionFit: Rope is made of twisted fibres called strands, and the Strand is a famous central London street.
